name: Dodge Viper GTS
description:
The Dodge Viper GTS, introduced in 1996, transformed the raw, street-legal race car concept of the original RT/10 roadster into a more refined and practical coupe without sacrificing its brutal performance character. The GTS became an instant icon with its distinctive 'double bubble' roof design—slightly raised sections that accommodated helmet clearance while paying homage to Pete Brock's legendary Shelby Daytona Coupe.

Despite sharing its basic silhouette with the RT/10, more than 90% of the GTS was new or significantly revised. The fixed roof coupe body provided improved aerodynamics and structural rigidity, while the iconic blue and white racing stripes became the car's signature look. Under the long hood sat the same massive 8.0-liter (7,990 cc) V10 engine, now tuned to produce 450 horsepower at 5,200 rpm and 664 Nm (490 lb-ft) of torque at 3,700 rpm.

The GTS represented a significant step forward in usability, becoming the first Viper equipped with airbags, air conditioning, power windows, and power door locks as standard equipment—amenities the spartan RT/10 lacked. Despite these creature comforts, the GTS remained a serious performance machine capable of genuine supercar acceleration and top speeds approaching 300 km/h.

The car's impact was immediate: it was chosen as the pace car for the 1996 Indianapolis 500, and it went on to dominate GT racing, winning its class at the 24 Hours of Le Mans multiple times. The GTS became the definitive first-generation Viper and remains one of the most iconic American sports cars ever built.
author: GeroDa74
